schemaNote: Fits are ordered slots. Roles: outer, layer, top, base, bottom, shoe, belt, accessory. 'position' is the layering/display order. itemId references wardrobe.json items[].id. 'id' is the database key and the only reliable one — 'code' survives only on the fits that were imported from the 2026-08-27 markdown.
renderNote: 'images' carries every picture of a fit and 'images.display' is the one a screen should draw. A hero or layered render is a GENERATED IMAGE, never a photograph of Max wearing the clothes, and images.heroIsGenerated says so. 'images.upload' is a picture Max uploaded in the app: it outranks the hero and is deliberately NOT labelled — whether it is a photograph or a render of his own is not recorded. images.looks is 2 only when a base/layered pair should be shown as a pair.
wardrobeNote: 'wardrobe' is derived from the occasion tags of a fit and its garments, exactly as the /fits screen derives it — it is not a stored flag. A fit is golf when it carries the golf occasion, or is built on a crested club garment.

fits.commentary: This is close to the literal uniform half the office wears. Grey polo is a true neutral, indigo denim is honest and current, the vest is completely normal here. Swap the polo for the Manfinity blue/mustard one for a bit more colour.

fits.catch: Coated jeans greying at thigh/seat. Check in daylight; swap to trousers_09_celio-indigo-jeans if the wear reads.

fits.name: Oatmeal & Navy Wool - sharp
fits.commentary: Best knit + best trouser + best shoe, never yet combined. Pale over dark at full strength.
fits.catch: Repair the Fedeli cuff hole and neck mark first. No black leather with navy wool.

preconditions.text: Repair the Fedeli cuff hole and neck mark first

fits.name: Blazer Over Burgundy - sharp
fits.commentary: The blazer is already the reflex jacket, but over trousers. Over jeans it reads made-an-effort instead of bank.
fits.catch: Blazer is full through the body - wear open, never buttoned.

fits.name: Cardigan & Brioni - everyday, elevated
fits.commentary: Pale-blue chambray collar out of a black cardigan is the best small detail owned, currently buried.
fits.catch: Brioni white has gone creamy - whiten-wash first. Cardigan open.

preconditions.text: Brioni white has gone creamy - whiten-wash first

fits.name: Navy Knit & Stone - everyday
fits.commentary: Only dark polo owned, knitted not pique so it reads a step smarter. Lowest-effort good outfit on the list.
fits.catch: Polo is size S - check it is not pulling. Never over navy bottoms.

fits.name: The Vest, Done Right - daily uniform, upgraded
fits.commentary: Highest-leverage change available - the vest goes on every winter day anyway. Cashmere under it instead of a polo; leather boot instead of a sneaker.
fits.catch: The boot is what stops this reading dad-at-the-hardware-store. With a sneaker it flattens.

fits.name: Sage & Tan - everyday, warm
fits.commentary: Sage is the most flattering polo colour and the fit benchmark of the synthetic set. The brogue blue sole caps the formality.
fits.catch: Nothing olive nearby - sage and olive go muddy. No-show socks.

fits.name: White polo & sage
fits.commentary: The cleanest warm-weather answer you own. Sage is a muted mid-tone, so white on top still has somewhere to sit.
fits.catch: No-show socks, and keep the loafers out of the wet - suede.

fits.name: Grey V-neck & cobalt
fits.commentary: The cobalt chino has been sitting unused because nothing obvious went with it. Grey is the one neutral that does not fight a saturated blue.
fits.catch: White tee, not grey - a grey tee under a grey V-neck reads like you got dressed in the dark.

fits.name: Blue V-neck & beige
fits.commentary: Beige is the best-fitting chino and underused. Mid-blue over it is the most conventional good-looking thing in this list, which is the point.
fits.catch: The brogue blue sole stops this reading country-English. Do not swap for the Church for this weather.

fits.name: Brioni & Air Max
fits.commentary: Best polo with sneakers and denim. High-low done deliberately - the Brioni collar carries the fit, the trainers stop it looking like you tried.
fits.catch: Whiten-wash the Brioni first; it has gone slightly creamy. Clean the Air Max - the toes are grubby.

preconditions.text: Whiten-wash the Brioni first; it has gone slightly creamy

fits.name: Brown cashmere & stone gingham
fits.commentary: Brown over pale stone with chestnut on the feet is a tonal fit that does not look like you were trying to make one.
fits.catch: Brown-on-brown needs the tones to differ. V-neck is warm mid-brown, the Church are chestnut - that gap is what makes it work. Do not use the brown Chelsea instead.

fits.name: Red V-neck & stone
fits.commentary: You own three reds and wear none. Red over pale stone is the easiest way in - the trouser is quiet enough that the colour does the work.
fits.catch: White tee only. A red tee under a red V-neck flattens both.

fits.name: Slate & black, under the biker
fits.commentary: Slate blue is the only cool mid-tone in the knitwear and it disappears under black well. All-dark from the waist down, one muted colour at the chest.
fits.catch: The coated jeans are greying at the thigh - check in daylight, swap to indigo if it reads.

fits.name: Raspberry & navy wool
fits.commentary: Raspberry cashmere over navy wool is the most grown-up colour pairing available, and neither piece gets used.
fits.catch: Brown leather only with navy wool - no black. The raspberry is a Tailor item; check it sits right before committing.

fits.name: Blue V-neck, vest, stone
fits.commentary: Your actual winter habit - vest over knit - but with a real colour under it instead of a grey polo, and a leather boot rather than a sneaker.
fits.catch: Slate vest over blue V-neck is two blues. If they read as one colour on you, swap the knit for the raspberry.

fits.name: Red under black
fits.commentary: Red cashmere framed by an open black cardigan, with a black tee closing the V. Three layers, one colour, held in a frame rather than shouted.
fits.catch: Cardigan open, always. Black tee, not white - white would cut the red into two pieces.

fits.name: Oatmeal & cobalt
fits.commentary: Best knit against the boldest thing in the wardrobe. Pale cashmere over saturated blue is a proper colour decision rather than a safe one.
fits.catch: Repair the Fedeli cuff and the neck mark first - this fit lives or dies on the knit looking expensive.

preconditions.text: Repair the Fedeli cuff and the neck mark first - this fit lives or dies on the knit looking expensive

fits.name: Pale blue, vest, black
fits.commentary: Pale blue over black is a sharper contrast than the pale-on-pale combinations the polo usually ends up in. The slate vest sits between the two tones.
fits.catch: The fit most likely to read generic. The black bottom half is what saves it - with a stone chino it is just another office polo.

fits.name: Burgundy & black
fits.commentary: Cashmere and trainers. The burgundy is the only colour in frame and the black bottom half makes it the whole point.
fits.catch: Clean the Air Max. On this fit the shoes are visible and the grubbiness shows.

fits.name: Club navy & loafers
fits.commentary: The club crest is why this knit is excluded from work fits. Off duty that stops mattering and it is just a good navy V-neck.
fits.catch: Navy over indigo is close. Without the white tee showing at the V it would read as one flat colour.

fits.name: Mustard & black
fits.commentary: The mustard tipping is the loudest thing you own and it is wasted against pale chinos. On black it becomes a deliberate accent.
fits.catch: Nothing else patterned. This polo is the pattern.

fits.name: Navy knit & beige
fits.commentary: The knit polo reads smart without a jacket, so it carries a bar or a dinner on its own. Beige and brown keep it warm rather than corporate.
fits.catch: Size S - check it is not pulling across the chest before you leave.

fits.name: Sage & black
fits.commentary: Sage is the most flattering colour in the polo set. Against black it stops being a summer colour and becomes a year-round one.
fits.catch: Nothing olive nearby - sage and olive go muddy. That rules out the Air Max on this fit.

fits.name: Biker & blue

items.note: tees_04_green-crew worn alone in place of the V-neck and tee, for a warmer evening

fits.catch: Wipe the jacket down. Worn open, always.

fits.name: Blazer over a V-neck
fits.commentary: Every existing blazer fit puts a crew neck under it. A V-neck with a white tee showing is a different register - softer, more Italian.
fits.catch: Blazer open. The white tee must sit clean at the V - if the neckline is stretched, this falls apart at the one point everyone looks.

fits.name: Overcoat over the shawl
fits.commentary: Texture on texture - chunky shawl collar inside a wool overcoat, aubergine just visible at the opening. Too formal for a normal office day, which is why it belongs here.
fits.catch: Spot-clean the mark near the left hip of the overcoat. Brown leather only with navy wool.

fits.name: Grey blazer & the yellow stripe

fits.name: Black dobby & the vest

fits.name: Brown cashmere over the brown stripe

fits.name: Leopard scarf & burgundy

fits.catch: The crinkle scarf undercuts tailoring - never with a blazer. The charcoal shirt needs the pale trouser to read, and no charcoal or grey knit over it.

fits.catch: Never the beige or stone chino - terracotta over beige goes flat and warm. Nothing over it, nothing else patterned. Worn tucked.

items.note: Invisible under a crew - recorded for laundry and availability, not for the render.

items.note: Sleeves pushed up, placket open at the top.
The olive is the only colour in the fit.

items.note: Sleeves pushed up, placket open at the top.

fits.catch: Same placket and sleeve rule. Keep every piece of leather brown. The epaulettes and the bomber sit in the same register, which is why this pairing works better than the henley does alone.

fits.name: Tan and cornflower

items.note: DRAPED over the shoulders, sleeves knotted at the chest - not worn. Swap for fedeli-cashmere-crew once its cuff is repaired.
Untucked, collar open, sleeves rolled to just below the elbow.
Turn-up cuff left as it is - on a tan chino short it reads considered, not dated.

fits.commentary: Tan and cornflower is a warm-cool pair that flatters Max without either half shouting, and the navy knit on the shoulders is the anchor that stops the whole thing floating away into pastel. Brown suede against tan cotton keeps the bottom half tonal so the eye goes to the shirt. Built for a Sydney marina or a harbourside lunch: cotton and linen throughout, because technical cloth reads as golf kit the moment it leaves a course.
fits.catch: The draped knit is a substitute. fedeli-cashmere-crew is the better choice - oatmeal cashmere over cornflower linen beats navy wool, and cashmere drapes where wool can sit stiff - but its verdict is Tailor: the cuff needs repairing and there is a mark at the neck. A shoulder drape puts the cuffs knotted in the middle of the chest, which is the worst place for a damaged cuff. Swap the Fedeli in once it is repaired.
fits.style: Riviera casual - quiet, warm-cool, nothing trying hard

fits.name: White, pale blue and burgundy

items.note: DRAPED over the shoulders, not worn. Its own note warns it is too roomy to wear over a polo - draped, that does not apply, and this is why it is on the shoulders here.
The pale blue contrast collar is the point - do not substitute a plain white polo.
Swap to shorts_17_chambray-linen-look if the slubbier cloth is wanted.
The one nautical reference in the outfit. Nothing else may add another.
Sockless. Brought into the rotation on 2026-08-30 for this fit.

fits.commentary: Burgundy against pale blue and white is the one properly French combination in this wardrobe, and it puts the colour where Max actually wants it: everywhere else in his summer clothes the shorts are the neutral and the top carries the colour, and here the draped knit takes that job instead. The navy-and-white webbing belt is the only overtly nautical thing in the outfit - one such item is charm, two is costume - so nothing else references boats.
fits.catch: Nothing blocking it. The navy suede driving moc this fit is built on used to be out of scope, marked holiday only; it was brought into the rotation on 2026-08-30 precisely so this fit could stand up. If it ever goes back out, the fallback is the brown suede loafer, and this fit then duplicates fit_m1_tan-and-cornflower.
fits.style: The louder harbourside option - colour in the draped knit, not the shirt

preconditions.text: Decide whether the navy suede driving moc comes back into rotation - it is currently scope = out, marked holiday only, and it is the shoe this fit is built on.

fits.name: Moto & burgundy

items.note: the faded pair actually worn on 25 Aug — see the catch
Swap for this when the indigo looks washed out — black coating under a black waxed biker is deliberate, not accidental.

fits.commentary: Burgundy against black does what it should. The jacket sits correctly at the hip with clean shoulders, and the Ecco disappears into the hem — correct behaviour for an all-black shoe. Reads current, not dated.
fits.catch: The jeans are the weak point: too faded to sit under all that black, so the eye lands on the worst garment, and the hem breaks and pools over the shoe. Swap to the black coated jean.
fits.style: Black on black, one warm note

fits.name: Fedeli and navy chino
fits.commentary: The Fedeli is flagged "best piece owned" and "pale neutral, so it needs a dark bottom to read at all", and until now the only navy under it was suit wool - so the best garment in the wardrobe was locked to one dressed-up look, fit_oatmeal_and_navy_wool. Same colour logic, register he can actually wear on a Saturday. Olive is named in the knit's own pairs line, which is what the Air Max brings.
fits.catch: Repair the Fedeli cuff hole and the neck mark first. Clean the Air Max - the toes are grubby. Hem the trouser. Webbing belt rather than leather: with a sneaker there is no leather to match and navy/white keeps it tonal. Swap to the brown chelsea and the distressed brown belt if it needs to survive a nice lunch.

fits.name: Pink Stripe and Navy Chino
fits.commentary: The shirt's own catalogue card asks for this trouser by name - "beige/stone chino with a black belt, navy chino, dark denim, worn open-collar, no tie". Navy, dusty pink and cognac is as safe as this gets while still being a choice. It is also the only place tops_12 can go without a blazer: its one other fit is fit_s3, grey blazer over navy wool, and in a Sydney September a rank-5 shirt with no jacket had no rank-4 bottom to sit on until this trouser turned up.
fits.catch: Hem the trouser first - it is 2-3cm long and breaks on the shoe. Shirt tucked, collar open, no tie. Do NOT add the Zara navy blazer: navy jacket on navy chino in two different cloths is the obvious way to wreck it. Swap the Church's for the brown chelsea if it needs to read younger.

fits.name: Jade & strawberry
fits.commentary: Jade and strawberry red sit opposite each other on the wheel, so the pairing reads as a decision rather than an accident. Cream shoe and cream-and-green cap stop it becoming a traffic light.
fits.catch: The only SEEN fit in trousers — it doubles as the loud chilly-morning option. Not for a 30-degree day.

fits.name: Orange & teal
fits.commentary: The cleanest loud pairing in the wardrobe. White polo referees it, and teal appears exactly twice — belt and shoe — bracketing the orange top and bottom.
fits.catch: Do not add a third colour. The teal belt and teal shoe are the whole structure.

fits.name: Red & azure
fits.commentary: Two primaries with a hard white break at the waist. Lime is the third colour, used twice — visor and shoe flash — and nowhere else; that repetition is what keeps it deliberate.
fits.catch: The white belt is load-bearing. Swap it for a coloured one and the red and blue start fighting.

fits.name: Coral riot
fits.commentary: The only fit in the batch where the print does the shouting, so everything below it goes quiet and dark. The indigo-violet belt picks up the polo's magenta collar.
fits.catch: Vest, not a quarter-zip — a sleeve over this print buries it. Alternate belt: the purple plastic one.

fits.name: Tour charcoal
fits.commentary: Dark top, white bottom, black visor, zero pattern anywhere. Nothing to look at, which is the point.
fits.catch: Keep the shoe grey or white. A coloured shoe undoes the whole register.

fits.name: Teal & slate
fits.commentary: The ELORD teal is muted enough to act as a neutral, so teal over slate is a two-step tonal move rather than a colour clash. Cream at the shoe and cap lifts it off drab.
fits.catch: Needs the cream accents. All-grey accessories and it goes flat.

fits.name: Grey with one navy note
fits.commentary: The grey-plus-one-colour rule at its strictest: grey polo, grey shoe, and navy used exactly three times.
fits.catch: Swap the navy short for a grey one and the fit dies. The navy is the only thing holding it up.

fits.name: Dusty rose & charcoal
fits.commentary: Dusty rose over charcoal is the most current thing in the wardrobe and reads as confidence rather than as a man in a pink shirt. Rescues a polo that fits nowhere else.
fits.catch: Charcoal below, nothing warmer. A tan or khaki short turns it sickly.

fits.name: Cream & tan
fits.commentary: All cotton, all warm neutrals, tartan hidden inside the waistband where it belongs. The rope cap is the only period detail doing any work.
fits.catch: Wool layer only. A technical quarter-zip over mercerised cotton kills the look instantly.

fits.commentary: Argyle is the one pattern allowed to be the whole idea, so nothing else patterns. Cream twill below, stone above, navy in the middle.
fits.catch: Blocked on replacing the cream twill short — see the precondition. Wool layer only.

fits.name: Masters green

items.note: optional — better WITH the layer than without

fits.commentary: Pine green over white is about as trad as golf gets. The red merino over dark green is the one combination in the batch that looks better with the layer than without it.

fits.name: Blue medallion
fits.commentary: Pale blue over salmon pink is straight 1980s American club preppy, and the single most old-school thing this wardrobe can build. Both garments cotton.
fits.catch: Do not add a technical anything. Wool layer or no layer.
